youtube.title: A Club of America's Richest Men Was Warned About Its Dam | The Johnstown Flood
youtube.description:
Above Johnstown, Pennsylvania, the South Fork Fishing and Hunting Club, whose members included Andrew Carnegie and Henry Clay Frick, owned an old earthen dam. It made cheap repairs, lowered the dam for a road, never replaced the drain pipes, and screened the spillway. Daniel Morrell of the Cambria Iron Company warned the club. On 31 May 1889, the dam failed and 2,209 people died. The club was never held liable.

📂 Case File #043: The Johnstown Flood
